title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Server Ping Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler writes an unmasked server ping, reads the client's pong, and then continues the same tunnel for a later text message and response.
preconditions: The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
The received ping/pong helper boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0005`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and regression tests pass, the new RFC 9220 server-ping requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified manual server ping behavior on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels while preserving the same stream for pong and later data. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
